Independent exact replay: N<=8, 58 multisets, 813 rows from grounded Laplacians match both original per-edge formulas. Separately group all positive integer partitions for N<=30 by (N,r) and maximize the rational row score over pairs; all 435 groups have the predicted unique multiset.
correctness.rationale: For the repaired claim, a known exact per-edge cut-projection row sum is 2+f_N(u)+f_N(v) for parts of sizes u,v. At fixed t=u+v, strict concavity forces the balanced integer split. For r>=3 and N>=5, each allowed increment of the balanced score equals f_N(k+1)-f_N(k) with k=floor(t/2)<=(N-2)/2, and its numerator is at least (N-2)(N-4)/4>0. The optimal t is therefore exactly N-r+2, leaving only singleton parts. For r=2 the sum is forced and for r>=3, N<=4 each fixed count has only one multiset. Substitution gives the optimized value, and the reciprocals sum to 4/N+O_r(N^-2), giving the correction r+6. In the original, the row identities themselves check out by solving the zero-mean vertex dipole and counting absolute differences; diagonal entry R>0 gives S_Q=S_P+1-2R. But the original proof line 110 makes a false comparison with the balanced bipartite graph at the same N (at N=5, K_{2,2,1} yields 26/15 versus K_{3,2} at 5/3); the original strict universal bounds instead follow directly from a+b<=N and R>0. Also, K_{N-2,1,1} has tied cut-projection edge orbits, so an attaining edge between largest parts need not be the only type. The replacement makes no cross-count comparison or claim about uniqueness of a norming edge.
residual_risks: Finite enumeration corroborates the proof only. Uniqueness is up to graph isomorphism/part permutation, not choice of edge.

value.rationale: The original per-graph formulas are known and would not justify acceptance by themselves. The remainder answers a natural worst-case design question for bounded edge error at specified vertex budget and number of vertex classes. The unique extremizer concentrates non-singleton mass into two almost equal groups, rather than balancing the entire partition, and the dependence of the optimized deficit on the prescribed number of classes is explicit. The proof of strict concentration and equality across all boundary counts is substantive beyond evaluating or tabulating one known norm.
residual_risks: Specific to canonical gradient fitting, unweighted complete multipartite graphs and fixed N,r. Does not optimize complementary cycle norms or other projections.
